chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who initiates the greeting (salam) is more deserving of God and His Messenger.

key_terms.أَوْلَى: More deserving, closer, more entitled — indicates greater divine favor and moral precedence
key_terms.السَّلَام: The Islamic greeting of peace ('As-salamu alaykum'), a sunnah act of worship and social bond
key_terms.الْبَادِي: The initiator, the one who acts first — emphasizes proactive virtue in social interaction

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about who is closer to God among those who exchange greetings?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the person who takes the initiative to give the Islamic greeting of peace (salam) holds a higher standing with God and the Prophet. This hadith encourages Muslims to be proactive in spreading peace and goodwill, as the one who greets first demonstrates the greater virtue of social warmth and humility. The 'closeness to God and His Messenger' here conveys superior moral rank and divine favor.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The initiator with the greeting (السَّلَامُ) is the closest of the people with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The initiator of the offering of the greeting of peace is closer to Allah and His Messenger.”
